international.title: UK food inflation could hit 5% next year, Bank of England says
international.summary: Sharp rise expected as cost pressures mount, with experts factoring in energy price cap hike and potential impact of El Niño Food price inflation in the UK could hit 5% next year, the Bank of England has said, despite rising less sharply than feared since the onset of the Iran war. The deputy governor Clare Lombardelli told MPs on the cross-party Treasury select committee: “Food price inflation is coming in under what we expected [it] to be, and in fact under what the industry expected it to be.” Continue reading...
